Intra-group conflict is a type of conflict that occurs within a single group when members hold differing opinions or ideas regarding how to achieve common goals, which can lead to internal divisions and hinder progress toward collective objectives (note 1.pdf).

To understand this, think of it like a sports team where all the players share the ultimate goal of winning the championship, but they argue intensely about the specific strategy or play-calling required to get there. Because they cannot agree on the method, the team becomes fragmented, and their performance suffers.

[AI-GENERATED EXAMPLE]
Imagine a student project group tasked with creating a presentation. While every member wants to earn an 'A' grade, two members believe they should focus on a creative video format, while the other two insist on a traditional slide deck. Because the group is stuck debating these different approaches rather than working on the content, they fail to make progress on the assignment, illustrating how intra-group conflict can stall collective success.
